evidence.quote: I believe that the appropriate time has not yet arrived, but I expect that conditions may warrant an increase in the federal funds rate target sometime this year.
If incoming data support such a forecast, the federal funds rate should be normalized, but at a gradual pace.
While there has been considerable progress on the maximum employment leg of our dual mandate, progress on the price stability leg has been notably absent.
But I think we can all agree that the recovery in the labor market has been substantial.
International experience therefore counsels caution in removing accommodation until the Committee is more confident that aggregate demand will continue to expand in line with its expectations
a significant pickup in incoming readings on core inflation will not be a precondition for me to judge that an initial increase in the federal funds rate would be warranted.

parsed.rationale: The Chair signals liftoff likely this year without waiting for inflation to rise, a hawkish shift from zero rates, but heavily emphasizes a gradual path, low equilibrium rates, and downside risks near the zero lower bound. On balance, the signal is roughly neutral with a slight hawkish tilt relative to the prevailing near-zero stance.
